title: What is MCP
sources: Model Context Protocol docs, 'What is MCP?' modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro (open-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems; 'USB-C port for AI applications'; supported by Claude, ChatGPT, Visual Studio Code, Cursor and others)
Model Context Protocol docs, 'Architecture overview' (host creates one client per server; JSON-RPC 2.0 data layer; servers expose tools, resources and prompts; stdio and Streamable HTTP transports)

Model Context Protocol docs, 'Security best practices' (local servers run with the client's privileges; clients must show the exact command and get explicit user approval before one-click local server setup)

Wikipedia, 'Model Context Protocol' (introduced by Anthropic in November 2024; tool poisoning described by Invariant Labs in April 2025: malicious instructions hidden in tool descriptions visible to the model but not to users) - secondary source

Example numbers: five apps and five tools is an illustration of the N x M integration problem; 25 vs 10 connections is simplified. The injected instruction on screen is a made-up example. 'Pick by need' is a rule of thumb, not a sourced claim.

lines.text: An AI app wants your calendar, your files and your tickets, so does it need custom code for every tool?
lines.caps: WANTS YOUR *CALENDAR | FILES, *TICKETS | *CUSTOM CODE | FOR EVERY *TOOL?

lines.text: Five apps and five tools used to mean twenty five connectors.
MCP, the Model Context Protocol, replaces them with one shared standard.
The app is the host, it runs a client per connection, and each tool sits behind a server.
lines.caps: THE APP IS THE *HOST | ONE *CLIENT PER CONNECTION | BEHIND A *SERVER

lines.text: A server offers tools to run, resources to read, and prompts to reuse.
lines.caps: *TOOLS TO RUN | *RESOURCES TO READ | *PROMPTS TO REUSE

lines.text: So a tool builds one server, and every app that speaks MCP can use it, which is why so many do.
lines.caps: BUILD *ONE SERVER | EVERY APP CAN *USE IT | WHY SO *MANY DO

lines.text: But here's the catch: a server runs with your permissions, and a bad tool description can hijack the model.
lines.caps: BUT HERE'S THE *CATCH | RUNS WITH YOUR *PERMISSIONS | A BAD *DESCRIPTION | CAN HIJACK THE MODEL

lines.text: So only install servers you trust, and review what they run.
lines.caps: ONLY SERVERS YOU *TRUST | REVIEW WHAT THEY *RUN

lines.text: Pick MCP when many apps need many tools; for one fixed integration, a plain API call is simpler.
lines.caps: PICK *MCP | MANY APPS, MANY TOOLS | ONE FIXED: PLAIN *API CALL
